tasks.prompt: Correct the four forms that prevent this passage from meaning “He gives me seed. We two have it. The birds hear us two”: Hine sęlð ic sǣd. Wit hæfst hit. Ðā fuglas hīerað ūre.
tasks.target_specification: Hē sęlð mē sǣd. Wit habbað hit. Ðā fuglas hīerað unc. Four corrections: subject, recipient, dual agreement, dual accusative.
tasks.target_old_english: Hē sęlð mē sǣd. Wit habbað hit. Ðā fuglas hīerað unc.
tasks.invalid_prompt_use_note: Four forms in the quoted learner prompt are intentionally used with wrong roles/agreement; their morphology is real. Required recognition of ūre does not license its use as an accusative.

tasks.prompt: Write three connected Old English sentences: say that the man had birds, that he gave them seed, and that he rested himself. Use a personal pronoun after introducing the man.
